text:
maria: quick sync — i'm drafting a compact API contract between the Evictor and the Compactor subsystems. goal: make async evict requests explicit, support probes (non-blocking), and define clear semantics for partial acceptance so callers can handle fallbacks. please skim and chime in.

maria: proposed (sketch):
```
EvictRequest {
  pages: [PageId],
  priority: u8,        // 0 (low) .. 255 (urgent)
  allow_blocking: bool, // probe vs forced
  live_hint: Option<u16>, // small lifetime hint for anti-thrashing
}
EvictResponse {
  accepted: [PageId],
  rejected: [PageId],
  reservation_token: Option<Token>, // for prepare/commit flow
  reason: Option<String>,
}
```

maria: semantics i had in mind: ack means pages are "queued for eviction" (i.e., reservation established) but not necessarily flushed to host yet. caller uses reservation_token to move to prepare/commit. rejected pages stay resident as-is.

aj: clarification — "queued" vs "non-resident" is critical. if ack==non-resident we will block kernel tails. we should be explicit: ack->queued, commit->non-resident. :thinking:

sam: +1. practical model: queued -> preparing (pin/lock) -> committed (non-resident). we should track these states in metrics. ack should NOT imply eviction completed.

maria: good — i'll change wording. also propose that evict/commit be idempotent and reservation_token encodes intended page set.

liz: important: gpu-side refs. our current gpu_refcount must be consulted before accept. evictor should reply REJECT_PINNED if refcount>0. otherwise we risk racing with kernels.

aj: another call-site thing: KV cache and model kv-cache must supply live_hint to avoid thrash (e.g., short-lived activations). maybe also support `migration_preference: migrate_to_host | compact_on_gpu` so caller can prefer migration over compaction.

maria: added field suggestion: `migration_pref: Option<String>` and response may include `anti_thrash_score: Option<u16>` to help callers back off.

sam: metrics we need: evict_attempts, evict_accept_rate, avg_time_queue_to_commit, reject_reasons histogram, compaction_pressure gauge. those will help tuning.

maria: implementation note: compactor MUST NOT hold OS-level page locks across async operations. design pattern: probe->prepare->commit. sequence: 
1) probe (allow_blocking=false) -> EvictResponse (accepted subset)
2) for accepted set: request prepare(reservation_token) which pins/reserves pages for short window
3) commit(reservation_token) -> do actual move/flush -> release token.

aj: edgecases: prepare failing -> caller must rollback and release reservation. partial acceptance means compactor should fall back to splitting large pages or migrating to host staging. we should define explicit fallback policy for caller libraries.

liz: also define error codes: OK, REJECT_BUSY, REJECT_PINNED, REJECT_TRY_AGAIN_LATER, ERR_INVALID_TOKEN, ERR_INTERNAL. keep small and actionable.

maria: agreed. i'll include semantic notes that REJECT_BUSY means transient (try backoff), REJECT_PINNED means caller should drop attempt or migrate alternatives.

sam: tests: need microbench for thrash pattern (hot working set with frequent probes) and correctness test with in-flight kernels that hold refs while eviction occurs. ensure commit is idempotent and safe to retry.

maria: action items: i'll open a tiny RFC/pr with the interface sketch + unit tests + microbench. who can review?

aj: i can review the API and integration tests. +1

liz: i'll own the pinned-page test harness and help validate refcount semantics.

deploy-bot: config-check passed on branch evict-api-contracts (build 4821) :white_check_mark:

maria: awesome, thanks everyone. i'll land a draft PR tomorrow and tag @aj @liz @sam. :rocket:
